corpus.evidence: fixtures come from real corpus shapes plus an adversarial wave; no vulnerable/safe corpus authored beside this record.

oracle.evidence: no independent decider. A structural clone detector (Type-2 clone detection on the AST, as jscpd or PMD-CPD do) is the right one, and would replace the text-similarity premise entirely.
oracle.command: score findings against jscpd on the same corpus

effectiveFp.evidence: not measured under the formal protocol, but the two classes the previous record NAMED as effective FPs are now out of scope by construction. Of the corpus findings, 1,961 were test code — a repeated it() block is not a maintenance defect, the repetition IS the test — and 507 files were machine-generated, every one carrying a banner. 2,076 -> 258. What remains has not been sampled.

reachability.evidence: not applicable in the taint sense.

duel.evidence: not scored against sonarjs no-identical-functions, the direct competitor.

adversarial.evidence: a wave of 9 deliberately-distinct pairs reported 6 as duplicates — every one differing by a single semantically load-bearing token (5000 vs 250, x+y vs x-y, === vs !==). Fixed by requiring an EXACT match below 120 normalised characters, since a ratio is weak evidence on a short body. Now 6/6 kept apart with both real duplicates still caught. UNMET until a second wave finds nothing new.

realSource.evidence: 8 pinned repositories. 3,530 -> 2,076 across five normalisation defects, then 2,076 -> 258 once the rule stopped reporting on code nobody edits (test files 52.9%, generated files the bulk of the rest). Measured against the local tree for the first time — before #612 the rig ran local plugins against the PUBLISHED devkit, so any number that depended on a devkit predicate described the last release.

partition.evidence: probed against cognitive-complexity and max-parameters, which visit the same function nodes. All three now share the devkit skipGeneratedFiles gate and the corpus splits cleanly: 258 / 227 / 74 with no rule subsuming another.

coverage.evidence: 100% statements / branches / functions / lines across eslint-plugin-maintainability, 389 tests.

throughput.evidence: not measured, and this rule is the one most likely to pay: the comparison is pairwise over every function in a file.

knownGaps.summary: the rule decides duplication by edit distance over normalised TEXT, not by structural clone detection.
knownGaps.why: text similarity conflates 'looks alike' with 'is the same logic'. The short-body exact-match rule patches the worst of it; the premise is unchanged.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: an AST-based Type-2 clone detector is prototyped and scored against the same corpus.

knownGaps.summary: below 120 normalised characters a near-duplicate that is NOT exact is no longer reported.
knownGaps.why: deliberate: on a short body a one-character difference is still 95%+ similar, so the ratio carries almost no information and reported 6 of 9 distinct pairs.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: structural clone detection replaces the ratio, making length irrelevant.

knownGaps.summary: CLOSED 2026-08-22. The rule skips a file that declares itself machine-generated.
knownGaps.why: the previous reopenWhen was "a generated-file heuristic exists in the devkit". It does: isGeneratedFile reads an @generated docblock or a "this code was generated by" banner in the LEADING comments. Decided by the file's own declaration, never by whether the path contains the word — src/generated-reports/summary.ts still reports. All 507 files it silenced carry a banner and all are in the one corpus repository that ships generated code; the other seven lost nothing.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a generated file is found that carries no banner and the class is large enough to matter, or ignoreGeneratedFiles proves to hide a defect someone would have fixed.

knownGaps.summary: the rule does not look at test files, which were 52.9% of its corpus findings.
knownGaps.why: ignoreTestFiles already defaulted true but matched a BASENAME regex, so a suite laid out as test/spec/**  with plain filenames — okta-auth-js, the largest single group — was never covered. Now uses the devkit isTestFilePath, which decides directories by exact path SEGMENT. A repeated it() block restates its setup so it reads independently when it fails; "extract to a reusable function" is advice nobody takes.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a user reports duplication in tests they would actually have refactored, or the effectiveFp sample finds actionable test-file findings.

notes: Seal record OPENED 2026-08-21. The adversarial wave found the FP direction here, where the other rules leaked recall — 6 of 9 distinct pairs called duplicates. UPDATED 2026-08-22: the generated-code gap this record opened with is closed, realSource re-measured at 258, partition met. Still OPEN — oracle, effectiveFp, duel, adversarial, behaviour, throughput and recorded are untouched, and the text-similarity premise stands.
